title: Integrative bioinformatics and machine learning approaches reveal oxidative stress and glucose metabolism related genes as therapeutic targets and drug candidates in Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Noor, Fatima; Aslam, Sidra; Piras, Ignazio S; Tremblay, Cecilia; Beach, Thomas G; Serrano, Geidy E
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用生物信息学和机器学习识别阿尔茨海默病氧化应激与糖代谢相关治疗靶点及药物，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common form of dementia, has treatments that slow but do not stop cognitive decline. Additional treatments are based on its pathogenic mechanisms are needed. Evidence has long highlighted oxidative stress and impaired glucose metabolism as crucial factors in AD pathogenesis. Therefore, in this study we aimed to find key AD pathogenic pathways combining genes involved in oxidative stress and glucose metabolism as well as potential small-molecule therapeutic agents. METHODS: Using autopsy brain RNA sequencing data (GSE125583) derived from the Arizona Study of Aging and Brain and Body Donation Program, AD-related genes were identified via differential gene expression, pathway and coexpression analysis. Oxidative stress and glucose metabolism genes were correlated to pinpoint module genes. GSE173955 was used an independent dataset was used for validation, conducting molecular docking, assessing hub genes for AD, and integrating machine learning approaches. RESULTS: We identified 13,982 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in AD patients. Through WGCNA coexpression analysis, 1,068 genes were linked to AD-specific modules. Pearson's correlation analysis highlighted 99 genes involved in oxidative stress and glucose metabolism. Overlap analysis of DEGs, module genes, and these metabolic genes revealed 21 key overlapping targets. PPI network and receiving operating curve (ROC) curve analyses then identified AKT1 and PPARGC1A as diagnostic hub genes for AD. Machine learning-based virtual screening of small molecules identified various inhibitors and enhancers with drug-like potential targeting AKT1 (upregulated) and PPARGC1A (downregulated), respectively. Among others, the Random Forest model was the most reliable for predicting molecular activity. Molecular docking further validated the binding affinities of these small molecules (inhibitors/enhancers) to AKT1 and PPARGC1A. CONCLUSION: This study identified AKT1 and PPARGC1A as potential therapeutic targets in AD. We discovered drug candidates with strong binding affinities, offering new avenues for effective AD treatment strategies.
abstract_zh: 背景：阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是最常见的痴呆形式，现有治疗可延缓但无法阻止认知衰退。基于其致病机制需要额外治疗。长期证据强调氧化应激和葡萄糖代谢受损是AD发病机制中的关键因素。因此，本研究旨在结合氧化应激和葡萄糖代谢相关基因，寻找AD关键致病通路及潜在的小分子治疗药物。方法：利用来自亚利桑那衰老与脑体捐赠项目（Arizona Study of Aging and Brain and Body Donation Program）的尸检脑RNA测序数据（GSE125583），通过差异基因表达、通路和共表达分析识别AD相关基因。将氧化应激和葡萄糖代谢基因相关联以定位模块基因。GSE173955作为独立数据集用于验证，进行分子对接、评估AD核心基因，并整合机器学习方法。结果：我们在AD患者中识别出13,982个差异表达基因（DEGs）。通过WGCNA共表达分析，1,068个基因与AD特异性模块相关。Pearson相关分析突出显示99个参与氧化应激和葡萄糖代谢的基因。DEGs、模块基因和这些代谢基因的重叠分析揭示了21个关键重叠靶点。PPI网络和受试者工作特征曲线（ROC）分析随后将AKT1和PPARGC1A确定为AD的诊断核心基因。基于机器学习的虚拟筛选小分子识别出多种具有药物样潜力的抑制剂和增强剂，分别靶向AKT1（上调）和PPARGC1A（下调）。其中，随机森林模型在预测分子活性方面最为可靠。分子对接进一步验证了这些小分子（抑制剂/增强剂）与AKT1和PPARGC1A的结合亲和力。结论：本研究将AKT1和PPARGC1A确定为AD的潜在治疗靶点。我们发现了具有强结合亲和力的候选药物，为有效的AD治疗策略提供了新途径。
